newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary wheat, maize futures continue to rise.
newsitem.headline: Hungary wheat, maize futures continue to rise.

text.p: Milling wheat and maize futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange continued to rise on Tuesday, traders said.
Milling wheat was boosted by unconfirmed news of increasing Serb demand for Hungarian wheat, which many traders doubted. But contracts rose 90 to 400 forints per tonne.
Only the illiquid March maturity was limit-up by the close while May, after large sales near limit-up, had risen just 90 forints by the end of the day.
This may already indicate the rising trend has lost steam, dealers said.
"I think we may go down in a few days,' said Robert Monostori of Agrimpex. "The rise in wheat and maize is not supported by fundamentals."
Hungary has hundreds of thousands of tonnes of 1996 wheat and maize for which traders have not yet seen buyers.
Wheat and maize prices have fallen thousands of forints this year, but an upward correction pushed them higher again in the past few days.
Almost all maize contracts firmed on Tuesday and finished 100 to 400 forints up. May closed at 18,000 forints, up 100 and November rose 100 forints to 18,500 but December fell 50 to end at 18,750.
Traders said the rising trend could reverse soon.
"Now the market is occupied by smaller companies," Vajo said. "Large ones are waiting for higher prices and then they push them down again."
